docs.title: Boundary recommendation
docs.text: Keep control, planning, and safety interfaces narrow and message-based. This reduces coupling between simulator, hardware, and higher-level behaviors.

docs.title: Branching
docs.text:
• Create feature branches from development
  • Keep pull requests focused and small when possible

docs.title: Before opening a pull request
docs.text:
Run all automated checks:

pre-commit run --all-files

docs.title: Commit style
docs.text:
Use clear commit messages with a scope prefix, for example:

  • hardware: improve motor timeout handling
  • sim: add mujoco contact debug view
  • docs: update control loop diagram

docs.title: Team conventions
docs.text:
• Prefer message/interface changes in humanoid_interfaces before cross-package rewrites
  • Document any new topic/service/action in docs
  • Add tests for all non-trivial behavior changes

docs.title: 1. Create and activate a virtual environment
docs.text:
Use your preferred method (venv, conda, etc.), then install dev tools:

pip install -r requirements-dev.txt

docs.title: 2. Install pre-commit hooks
docs.text: pre-commit install

docs.title: 3. Run checks manually
docs.text: pre-commit run --all-files

docs.title: 4. Build docs locally
docs.text:
python -m mkdocs serve

Then open the local URL shown by MkDocs.

docs.title: Python API Standards (Team Checklist)
docs.text: Use this checklist when writing or modifying Python code so API docs remain useful and python -m mkdocs build --strict stays green.

docs.title: 1) Add type annotations for all public APIs
docs.text:
Include type hints for:

  • Function/method parameters
  • Return values
  • Public dataclass fields / attributes where practical

Example:

def compute_torque(q: np.ndarray, dq: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    ...

docs.title: 2) Write docstrings for public modules, classes, and functions
docs.text:
Use triple-quoted docstrings and describe:

  • Purpose
  • Key arguments
  • Return value
  • Units and coordinate frames for robotics quantities

Example:

def step(self, dt: float) -> None:
    """Advance simulation by one time step.

    Args:
        dt: Step size in seconds.
    """

docs.title: 3) Keep signatures stable and explicit
docs.text:
• Avoid overly-generic *args/**kwargs for public APIs unless necessary.
  • If needed, explain forwarded arguments in docstrings.

docs.title: 4) Document shapes and conventions
docs.text:
For vectors/matrices, include shape and meaning in docstrings:

  • q: (n_joints,) joint positions [rad]
  • J: (6, n_joints) geometric Jacobian

docs.title: 5) Avoid undocumented magic values
docs.text:
• Replace literals with named constants.
  • Explain thresholds/tolerances in docstrings or comments.

docs.title: 6) Keep imports and formatting clean
docs.text:
Before commit, run:

pre-commit run --all-files

This runs Ruff, mypy, clang-format, and docs validation hooks.

docs.title: 7) Add a minimal usage example for new core APIs
docs.text:
For important new classes/functions, add a short example in:

  • docs/api/python.md for API visibility, or
  • package README/docs page for workflow context.

docs.title: 8) Treat docs build as a required quality gate
docs.text:
Always ensure this passes locally before PR:

python -m mkdocs build --strict

docs.title: RobotModel
docs.text:
Bases: KinematicsMixin, CentroidalMixin, DynamicsMixin, SnapshotMixin

Central Pinocchio model interface for the MAX humanoid robot.

The robot is modeled as a floating-base system.

Responsibilities: - load the robot URDF - build the Pinocchio model - create and own the Pinocchio Data object - store the current robot state (q, v, a) - provide joint/frame information - provide the common model interface used by other modules

docs.text: Solve iterative inverse kinematics for a robot frame.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
frame_name : str Target frame.

target

If task='position': 3D target position, 4x4 pose, or pin.SE3.

If task='pose': 4x4 pose or pin.SE3.

array_like, optional

Initial configuration. Defaults to the current RobotModel q.

{'position', 'pose'}

Position-only or full SE(3) inverse kinematics.

iterable of str, optional

Joints allowed to move.

By default, joints in the kinematic chain of the target frame are used, excluding the floating-base root joint.

bool

Keep root_joint fixed by default.

int

Maximum CLIK iterations.

float

Position convergence tolerance in meters.

float

Orientation convergence tolerance in radians.

float

Integration step size.

float

Damped least-squares regularization.

bool

Clamp scalar active joints to model position limits.

docs.title: Returns
docs.text: dict { 'q': solution configuration, 'success': bool, 'iterations': int, 'task': str, 'active_joints': list, 'position_error': float, 'orientation_error': float or None, }

docs.title: Notes
docs.text: This solver uses a dedicated Pinocchio Data object. RobotModel.q, v, a and the shared self.data are not modified.

docs.title: DynamicsMixin
docs.text:
Rigid-body dynamics computations for the robot.

All computations use the current state stored in RobotModel.

docs.title: Conventions
docs.text:
Mass matrix: Shape (nv, nv)

Generalized forces

Shape (nv,)

Dynamic equation

tau = M(q) @ a + nle(q, v)

where

nle(q, v) = Coriolis/centrifugal effects + gravity

docs.title: coriolis_forces()
docs.text:
Return Coriolis and centrifugal generalized forces.

c(q, v) = C(q, v) @ v

docs.title: Returns
docs.text: numpy.ndarray Generalized Coriolis/centrifugal force vector with shape (nv,).

docs.title: coriolis_matrix()
docs.text:
Return the Coriolis matrix C(q, v).

The rigid-body dynamics equation is:

tau = M(q) @ a + C(q, v) @ v + g(q)

docs.title: Notes
docs.text: Pinocchio's computeCoriolisMatrix() modifies several fields of its Data object. Therefore, a dedicated Data object is used here so that computing C(q, v) does not corrupt cached kinematic or centroidal quantities stored in self.data.

docs.title: Returns
docs.text: numpy.ndarray Coriolis matrix with shape (nv, nv).

docs.title: forward_dynamics(tau)
docs.text: Compute generalized acceleration using ABA.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: tau : array_like Generalized force vector with shape (nv,).

docs.title: gravity()
docs.text: Return generalized gravity vector g(q).

docs.title: inverse_dynamics(acceleration=None)
docs.text:
Compute generalized forces using RNEA.

tau = M(q) @ a + nle(q, v)

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: acceleration : array_like, optional Generalized acceleration. If omitted, the current RobotModel acceleration is used.

docs.title: inverse_mass_matrix()
docs.text: Return inverse joint-space inertia matrix M(q)^-1.

docs.title: kinetic_energy()
docs.text: Return kinetic energy of the robot.

docs.title: mass_matrix()
docs.text: Return joint-space inertia matrix M(q).

docs.title: mechanical_energy()
docs.text:
Return total mechanical energy.

mechanical = kinetic + potential

docs.title: nonlinear_effects()
docs.text:
Return nonlinear effects vector nle(q, v).

Includes: - Coriolis effects - centrifugal effects - gravity

docs.title: potential_energy()
docs.text: Return gravitational potential energy of the robot.

docs.title: humanoid_utils.filters
docs.text: State-estimation filters.

docs.title: EKF
docs.text:
Bases: KF

Discrete-time Extended Kalman Filter.

The filter follows the nonlinear model

x_k = f(x_{k-1}, ...)
z_k = h(x_k, ...)

with covariance propagation based on the Jacobians F, L, H, and M.

docs.title: __init__(x0, P0, f, F, Q, L=None)
docs.text:
Initialize the Extended Kalman Filter.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default x0 Any

Initial state estimate.

required P0 Any

Initial estimation-error covariance.

required f Callable[..., Any]

Discrete nonlinear process model.

required F Model

State Jacobian of the process model.

required Q Any

Process-noise covariance.

required L Optional[Model]

Process-noise Jacobian/gain matrix. If None, additive process noise is assumed and L = I.

None

docs.title: predict(*args, **kwargs)
docs.text:
Perform the EKF prediction step.

Computes

x^- = f(x^+, ...)
P^- = F P^+ F^T + L Q L^T

Additional positional and keyword arguments are forwarded to the process model and its Jacobians.

docs.title: update(z, h, H, R, M=None, residual=None, *args, **kwargs)
docs.text:
Perform the EKF measurement-update step.

Computes

innovation = z - h(x^-)
S = H P^- H^T + M R M^T
K = P^- H^T S^-1
x^+ = x^- + K innovation

The covariance is updated using the Joseph stabilized form.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default z Any

Measurement vector.

required h Callable[..., Any]

Nonlinear measurement model.

required H Model

Measurement-model state Jacobian.

required R Any

Measurement-noise covariance.

required M Optional[Model]

Measurement-noise Jacobian/gain matrix. If None, additive measurement noise is assumed and M = I.

None residual Optional[Callable[..., Any]]

Optional custom residual function. This is useful for quantities such as wrapped angles.

None

Additional positional and keyword arguments are forwarded to h, H, and M.

docs.title: LKF
docs.text:
Bases: KF

Discrete-time Linear Kalman Filter.

The filter follows the linear model

x_k = F x_{k-1} + G u_{k-1} + w_{k-1}
z_k = H x_k + v_k

with

w ~ (0, Q)
v ~ (0, R)

docs.title: __init__(x0, P0, F, Q, G=None)
docs.text:
Initialize the Linear Kalman Filter.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default x0 Any

Initial state estimate.

required P0 Any

Initial estimation-error covariance.

required F Model

State-transition matrix.

required Q Any

Process-noise covariance.

required G Optional[Model]

Optional control-input matrix.

None

docs.title: predict(u=None, *args, **kwargs)
docs.text:
Perform the LKF prediction step.

Computes

x^- = F x^+ + G u
P^- = F P^+ F^T + Q

If no control input is used:

x^- = F x^+

docs.title: update(z, H, R, *args, **kwargs)
docs.text:
Perform the LKF measurement-update step.

Computes

innovation = z - H x^-
S = H P^- H^T + R
K = P^- H^T S^-1
x^+ = x^- + K innovation

The covariance is updated using the Joseph form.

docs.title: SRCKF
docs.text:
Bases: KF

Discrete-time Square-root Cubature Kalman Filter.

This implementation follows the SRCKF formulation used in the supplied MATLAB Q3 exercise.

The filter uses 2n cubature points

zeta = sqrt(n) * [I, -I]

and stores a lower-triangular square-root covariance factor

P = sqrt_P @ sqrt_P.T

Process and measurement noises are assumed additive.

docs.text: Initialize the Square-root Cubature Kalman Filter.

docs.text: Perform the SRCKF time-update step.

docs.title: reset(x0, P0)
docs.text: Reset state and square-root covariance.

docs.title: update(z, h, R, residual=None, measurement_mean=None, *args, **kwargs)
docs.text: Perform the SRCKF measurement-update step.

docs.title: SRUKF
docs.text:
Bases: UKF

Square-root UKF following the MATLAB Q3 SRUKF-style algorithm.

The filter stores a lower-triangular square-root covariance factor sqrt_P such that

P = sqrt_P @ sqrt_P.T

For consistency with the supplied MATLAB implementation, covariance matrices are reconstructed during prediction and update and are then re-factorized using a numerically safe Cholesky decomposition.

docs.title: dcm_to_quaternion(T)
docs.text: Convert a 3x3 DCM to a scalar-first quaternion.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: T : array-like, shape (3, 3) Direction cosine / transformation matrix using the same convention as quaternion_to_dcm().

docs.title: quaternion_to_rotation_matrix(q)
docs.text:
Convert a scalar-first quaternion to a 3x3 rotation matrix.

This implements the rotation tensor R given in Eq. (348) of the lecture notes.

docs.title: Parameters

docs.title: Returns

docs.title: rotation_matrix_to_quaternion(R)
docs.text: Convert a 3x3 rotation matrix to a scalar-first quaternion.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: R : array-like, shape (3, 3) Rotation matrix using the same convention as quaternion_to_rotation_matrix().

docs.title: Returns
docs.text:
numpy.ndarray, shape (4,) Unit quaternion:

    [q0, q1, q2, q3]

docs.title: Notes
docs.text: q and -q represent the same physical rotation. This function selects a representation with non-negative q0 when possible.
